items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: I was working with Herman Chittison, you know, great piano player and accompanist.

ctx.x: I certainly wouldn't agree with that statement in terms of quality.

Yeah, yeah, popularity. It wasn't that easy, and as I said before, I came off the road and I went into Le Ruban Bleu. So, I guess I was sort of isolated from the mainstream as when it came to making recordings and... I didn't do any radio then, and I was pretty exclusive. So I didn't get a chance to make any recordings,-- along with the shortage of material and all that. But this Joe Davis outfit and the musicians -- Well Cedric Wallace evidently had access to Joe Davis' publishing, and these are some of the…
You mentioned him before as part of Herman Chittison Trio.

items.title: 61529_Maxine Sullivan oral history interview
items.q: I lost track of Chit for awhile... the last time I saw Chitison he was doing very well

ctx.x: I guess Red Norvo. Red Norvo was with Teddy Wilson.

That's right. I lost track of Chit for awhile. He was - he did finally go out on the road with a singer and the last time I saw Chitison he was doing very well and I think he had made some commercial recordings. But I've never heard them. I don't know what he did.
I have an LP by him which is privately issued. I think his widow was taken around to jazz conferences.
